transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Recorded: yes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Alvarez (Montclair Head of Security), Maya Patel (Montclair SRE), Ethan Ross (Montclair Product), Liam Torres (Montclair Legal)

Summary (auto): quick intake focusing on identity, crypto, logging, and retention requirements for a retail customer with PCI-adjacent workloads. Agreed to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and run a mini benchmark.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, um this is Alex on the account side, i'm joined by Priya from our infra team. could we do quick intros?
00:14 Jordan Alvarez: yeah, i'm jordan, head of security for montclair, we handle payments and loyalty so there's some pci considerations, uh nice to meet you both.
00:22 Maya Patel: maya, s-r-e, mostly ops and deployment ownership.
00:26 Ethan Ross: ethan, product, i'll own success criteria for the pilot.
:30 Liam Torres: liam from legal, i'll be watching compliance bits.
00:35 Priya Shah: great, quick agenda: identity and sso, key management and encryption, rbac and token access, audit logs and retention, then tradeoffs between hosted/dedicated/private and pilot next steps. sound okay?
00:47 Jordan Alvarez: yep, that's exactly what we wanted. starting with SSO: we use Okta, we need SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning and groups mapped to roles, does redwood support full SAML flows and SCIM?
01:05 Priya Shah: yes, we have SAML2.0 with SP-initiated and IDP-initiated flows, SCIM v2 for provisioning. couple notes though — for hosted accounts we manage the control plane but support SAML/SCIM. for private deployment, customer IdP traffic stays in VPC if you want.
01:29 Jordan Alvarez: ok, so for hosted there is still an external control plane, how do we guarantee tokens and credentials for models aren't accessible by redwood engineers?
01:40 Alex Chen: good question. for hosted we use tenant isolation; engineers don't have plaintext model keys, everything's hashed/encrypted and access is audited. that said, if you need absolute separation, dedicated or private with customer-managed KMS is the option.
01:58 Maya Patel: can you explain customer-managed KMS? we have an HSM-backed KMS in our cloud.
02:06 Priya Shah: sure. two options: bring-your-own-key in the cloud KMS — we integrate via KMS key policies and envelope encryption so Redwood never stores the root key; or for private on-prem we can wire HSM directly and the key material never leaves your network. there are some tradeoffs on key rotation and latency.
02:30 Jordan Alvarez: any SOC2/ISO artifacts we can review now?
02:34 Alex Chen: yes, i'll send the SOC2 Type II report and our ISO27001 certificate. i'll add a short redwood-audit-summary doc with the controls most relevant to inference: model access controls, key management integration, and logging.
02:50 Ethan Ross: and retention — we need logs kept for 2 years for some investigations; what retention options do you give for audit logs and transmitted request traces?
03:03 Priya Shah: default is 90 days in hosted for audit logs, but we offer extended retention as an add-on; for dedicated you can configure log forwarding to your SIEM and choose retention — for private you control retention fully. export formats are JSON and syslog.
03:22 Liam Torres: is there a way to get immutable archives for compliance?
03:26 Priya Shah: we support WORM-style export to S3 for audit trails; for hosted we can ship snapshots to an S3 bucket you control or to your archive storage.
03:36 Jordan Alvarez: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles: developer, operator, analyst, model-deploy. can tokens be scoped to per-model permissions and per-route?
03:48 Priya Shah: yes, token-level scoping is supported. API keys can be scoped by model, route, and TTL. we also support role-based access in the console via groups mapped from SCIM. there are sometimes gaps in older console UI but enforcement is at the API/gateway layer.
04:12 Jordan Alvarez: what about audit events — do you log token usage, key rotations, and access to KV cache?
04:20 Priya Shah: we log auth events, key ops (rotate/create/destroy), and administrative actions. we don't log model KV contents — that's considered sensitive and never persisted in plaintext to logs.
04:34 Maya Patel: latency concerns — if we use customer-managed KMS for every inference call, do we risk high latency per token?
04:42 Priya Shah: we use envelope encryption and cache DEKs (data encryption keys) to avoid KMS roundtrips per token. KMS is used for DEK wrap/unwrap during session creation or rotation, so steady-state latency impact is negligible.
05:00 Ethan Ross: how about network access when using Private vs Dedicated — can we lock traffic to our VPC only?
05:10 Priya Shah: in private deployments yes, the control plane can be air-gapped and the inference nodes live in your VPC with security groups allowing only your subnets. for dedicated we offer VPC peering and IP allow lists; hosted is public endpoints with mTLS between runtime and control plane.
05:35 Jordan Alvarez: regulatory note: some of our customers are EU-only, we need data residency. do you have regional deployments?
05:44 Alex Chen: yes, we have regions in eu-west and us-east, you can pin routes and models to region. for strict residency we recommend private or dedicated in the region.
06:00 Liam Torres: encryption-at-rest — who holds the key by default?
06:05 Priya Shah: by default Redwood-managed KMS holds the root; you can bring your own key via customer KMS for hosted (we integrate with AWS/GCP/Azure KMS) or use customer-managed keys in dedicated/private.
06:20 Jordan Alvarez: auditability — can we get a sample of the log schema? we need to see fields and timestamps for forensics.
06:27 Priya Shah: yes i'll attach the audit schema doc but quick answer: events include actor, action, resource, timestamp, outcome, request-id, origin-ip.
06:36 Jordan Alvarez: great. also can you show us how RBAC ties to the console and CLI?
06:42 Priya Shah: console role mapping is SCIM group to platform role; CLI uses scoped API tokens and those are subject to the same role checks. I'll demo a quick flow in the pilot if helpful.
07:00 Ethan Ross: speaking of pilot, our goals: validate latency under typical traffic, confirm data retention and delete workflows, and prove KMS integration. target duration 2 weeks, low-volume. is that reasonable?
07:15 Alex Chen: yes, 2-week pilot is common. we'd provision a small dedicated pool or private sandbox depending on final choice. Priya, any red flags?
07:23 Priya Shah: no red flags. for the perf aspect we'll need sample request mix and payload sizes. if they're heavy multi-turn chats, batching and kv cache behavior matters.
07:34 Maya Patel: our payloads include images meta and some user PII; is there PII scrubbing options?
07:42 Priya Shah: we can configure pre-ingest filters or tokenization rules, and redact fields on ingestion; we also recommend not storing raw PII in prompt history and using ephemeral KV entries when needed.
07:58 Jordan Alvarez: incident response — what's Redwood's RTO/RPO SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
08:06 Alex Chen: hosted has a 99.9% uptime SLO and we offer incident pages and postmortems; dedicated carries an SLA option with tighter targets and faster incident escalation. private is customer-managed, Redwood supports ops but SLA depends on the agreed contract.
08:28 Liam Torres: do you do pen tests and vuln disclosures?
08:31 Alex Chen: yes we run quarterly pentests, internal and external, and we'll share the summary and our disclosure program.
08:40 Jordan Alvarez: about logs again — we want the ability to pull raw logs on demand for a forensics window, is that supported?
08:46 Priya Shah: yes for dedicated/private you can run ad-hoc exports to your S3 or SIEM; hosted customers can request exports, but there are rate and privacy constraints.
08:58 Ethan Ross: competitors question — we looked at MajorCloudAI and OnPremify. OnPremify promises complete in-house control but it's a lot of ops. what's the Redwood sweet spot?
09:10 Alex Chen: our sweet spot is predictable inference with ops handled but with the option to move to private if you need full control. Dedicated is the middle ground for predictable throughput and isolation.
09:22 Jordan Alvarez: any examples of customers in retail/commerce doing similar setups?
09:28 Alex Chen: yes, a footwear retailer used dedicated with BYOK KMS and two-year log retention in S3 for audits; I'll anonymize the case study and share.
09:38 Maya Patel: curious on RBAC primitives — do you support conditional roles based on IP or time of day?
09:44 Priya Shah: we have IP-based allow lists and token TTLs; time-based conditions are on the roadmap but not GA.
09:54 Jordan Alvarez: where do secrets for model endpoints live? e.g., environment variables, config secrets.
10:00 Priya Shah: secrets are stored encrypted in our secret store, backed by KMS; for BYOK the secret store wraps with your DEK. access to secrets is audited and requires role checks.
10:12 Ethan Ross: what about model provenance and tampering detection?
10:17 Priya Shah: we store model hashes and provenance metadata and provide signed manifests for models; for private you can control the model artifact store directly.
10:28 Jordan Alvarez: questions from legal — data subject requests and deletion flows, can you demonstrate?
10:33 Alex Chen: we have an admin flow to scrub user data from logs and from persisted prompt history; for hosted we run a deletion pipeline that purges records on request and returns an audit token of deletion. we'll need to map your retention classes to the pipeline.
10:50 Liam Torres: do you support DSR automation? like automated deletion on request via API?
10:55 Priya Shah: yes, we have DSR APIs that connect to our retention engine; for hosted customers we operate the pipeline, for private you run it.
11:08 Jordan Alvarez: ok good. another point: key rotation cadence — what's recommended and how disruptive is rotation for long-running sessions?
11:17 Priya Shah: recommended rotation is 90 days for root keys; because of envelope encryption, rotation is non-disruptive to existing sessions; we re-wrap DEKs and keep sessions valid until the DEK TTL expires.
11:32 Ethan Ross: for the pilot, we want to simulate 100 qps with bursts to 400 qps, is Redwood able to do that in dedicated?
11:40 Priya Shah: yes with burst capacity and autoscaling, dedicated pools can handle that; we'll size the pool during scoping and provide expected latency percentiles.
11:52 Jordan Alvarez: does the telemetry expose token-level cost and latency per token? we want to attribute spend to product features.
11:59 Alex Chen: yes our Console has token-level cost breakdown and per-request latency histograms, plus route-level dashboards. we can give you API access to the telemetry for billing integration.
12:18 Ethan Ross: is there a limit on how long we can keep KV cache entries?
12:24 Priya Shah: TTLs are configurable, but for privacy reasons it's recommended to keep them short for PII. entries can be ephemeral and evicted automatically.
12:38 Jordan Alvarez: do you support field-level encryption in request payloads?
12:43 Priya Shah: some customers use client-side encryption for sensitive fields prior to sending; Redwood can accept encrypted blobs and treat them as opaque. field-level server-side encryption is possible with custom transforms in private deployments.
12:58 Maya Patel: network ingress/egress audit — does Redwood provide egress logs showing external destinations?
13:05 Priya Shah: we do for dedicated and private; for hosted we log outbound destinations for third-party connectors but not full packet captures.
13:22 Jordan Alvarez: can we show a sample of the SCIM group mapping to roles?
13:27 Priya Shah: yes, sample mapping will be in the SCIM guide I'll share.
13:34 Ethan Ross: timechecks — we're at about 13 minutes in, can we fast-forward to key decision points?
13:40 Alex Chen: sure. decision drivers seem to be: absolute key ownership and residency pushing toward private, throughput/cost concerns pushing toward dedicated, and speed-to-value pushing toward hosted.
13:54 Jordan Alvarez: yes, that captures it. quick thing — do you support MFA for API key issuance and admin console?
14:01 Priya Shah: we support MFA for console admins and strong token lifecycles for API; we're adding hardware MFA for elevated admin actions.
14:14 Liam Torres: audit trail chain of custody — can we get signed audit manifests for legal holds?
14:21 Alex Chen: we can produce signed manifests for exported archives and timestamps for chain-of-custody.
14:30 Jordan Alvarez: on the encryption note, we need assurance that model outputs aren't included in logs. you said prompt history is separate — can that be completely disabled?
14:40 Priya Shah: yes, prompt history persistence can be disabled or set to ephemeral; and we can mask outputs in logs. default analytics may still keep anonymized metrics.
14:56 Ethan Ross: any limitations on model quantization or custom kernels in private?
15:04 Priya Shah: private gives more flexibility for custom runtimes, but certain kernel optimizations depend on hardware—our engineering team can collaborate during onboarding.
15:20 Jordan Alvarez: compliance packs — do you have a PCI adjacent checklist for inference workloads?
15:26 Alex Chen: we have an industry pack that outlines controls for cardholder-adjacent data handling; i'll include it in the artifact packet.
15:34 Maya Patel: about ops — what's the escalation path during incidents on dedicated pools?
15:39 Priya Shah: dedicated includes an oncall rotation; customers get a dedicated operations contact and a pager channel and runbook.
15:48 Ethan Ross: can we get telemetry exported to our prometheus and datadog stacks?
15:53 Priya Shah: yes, we have exporters and push/prometheus integrations for metrics; logs go to SIEMs.
16:06 Jordan Alvarez: are there any known constraints around VPC peering for our cloud vendor? we use GCP primarily.
16:13 Priya Shah: we support GCP VPC peering and private service connect patterns; sometimes there are quota/network constraints on peering which we help troubleshoot.
16:26 Liam Torres: for the contract, do you require indemnities around model outputs?
16:31 Alex Chen: standard terms vary — we'll surface indemnity language and liability caps; for enterprise we can discuss tailored language.
16:42 Jordan Alvarez: ok, to wrap up what we'll need from you: SOC2/ISO artifacts, SCIM guide, audit schema, KMS integration doc, sample RBAC mappings, and a perf/cost sheet for the dedicated pilot.
16:55 Alex Chen: yep, we'll bundle that. Priya will run the perf bench and I'll add the compliance docs.
17:02 Ethan Ross: timeline — if we get artifacts by next week can we kick pilot the week after?
17:07 Alex Chen: yes, assuming contract language is aligned.
17:10 Liam Torres: we'll need to review redlines but aim to move quickly.
17:15 Jordan Alvarez: anything else?
17:18 Priya Shah: one more note on operational isolation — for dedicated we can set up scheduled backups of logs to your S3 with encryption-by-key and retention rules matching your policy.
17:30 Jordan Alvarez: great, that's helpful. okay thanks everyone, we'll look for the docs and schedule the next meeting to align pilot scope.
17:38 Alex Chen: thanks folks, closing notes: send artifacts, then sync on pilot scoping call.
17:45 (call ends)

Notes: There are a few transcription artifacts — speaker labels sometimes overlap; some acronyms were transcribed as separate letters (K-M-S). Links referenced to be shared in follow-up: SOC2 packet, SCIM guide, audit log schema, dedicated perf/cost spreadsheet.
